problems: The caption says 'as I carry the magnet stone', but the black stone is never in the bird's beak or feet: in the storyboard (frames 1-12) and the 25% and 75% frames it sits or slides on the grass on its own, apart from the bird's legs. It moves right to left with nothing touching it.
The bird is cut off by the top edge in every frame, so its head is never seen and a viewer can't tell who is doing anything.

The whole film is very dark. The bowl, the lily pad and the thin needle are dim and small in the middle of the frame, and the stone is a black block on dark grass that is hard to find (75% frame, left edge).
The needle does turn (it points a different way at 25%, 50% and 75%), but since the stone slides by on its own, a viewer can't see what makes it turn.
posts.critique: The needle turns, but the stone that should cause it glides across the grass by itself while a bird with no head walks behind. The scene is too dark and too badly framed to follow.

problems: The subject named in the title, a top floating over a lodestone ring, is never shown. The grey ring in the background (right side, every storyboard frame) is empty from start to end.
A big striped top fills the middle of every frame. It stands motionless on a black disc, and its handle is cut off by the top edge of the frame.

The caption admits the wrong thing is in front, but this is a framing failure, not a failed experiment. Nothing happens for 10 seconds except leaf shadows moving and orange legs passing at the edge (storyboard frames 12-14, 75% frame top right).
posts.critique: Ten seconds of a still striped top blocking the view, with an empty ring behind it. The post tells you itself that it doesn't show what it is about.

problems: 'My magnet stone goes past' suggests someone carries it, but the black cube slides across the grass by itself next to the bird's feet (storyboard frames 1-16). It is never in a beak or foot, and nothing pushes it.
The bird is only ever visible as cropped legs and belly at the top-left edge. Its feet seem to stand still while the cube and the camera drift.

The 'iron spikes' are thin dark lines barely visible on the grass (25% frame). At the end (75% frame, storyboard frames 13-16) the red sticks go through the cube and stick out both sides instead of clinging to its surface, which is clipping.
The dark tree shadow covers the first half, which makes the cube and spikes hard to see.
posts.critique: A black box slides along on its own next to a pair of cropped legs, and the spikes that should cling to it end up stuck through it. The cause, the contact and the framing all fail.
